diagnostic_bottleneck: None; early-stage honeydew exudate on panicle is a distinct hallmark of Ergot, clearly differentiating it from other candidates which lack this specific symptom or location.

final_decision.reason: The presence of viscous, amber-colored honeydew exudate on the panicle florets is a classic early-stage symptom of Ergot (Claviceps purpurea). Other candidates like Smut, Rust, Blast, and Leaf Spots are contradicted by the absence of spore masses, pustules, or necrotic lesions, and the specific location/symptom type. Downy Mildew is unlikely due to the absence of green ear transformation.

symptom_class.description: Viscous, amber-colored fluid oozing from the florets and forming droplets.

geometry.shape: panicle is cylindrical; individual florets are grain-shaped
geometry.deformation: Florets appear intact but are coated and connected by exudate.

surface.features: Droplets of fluid visible hanging from the panicle.

texture.description: The surface of the panicle is slick and reflective due to the exudate.

distribution.pattern: Diffuse across the visible panicle surface

reproductive_structure.details: Florets are present but obscured by exudate. No obvious replacement by sclerotia or smut balls visible in this view.

uncertain: Internal condition of grains (obscured by exudate)
